newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Incitec sees subdued second half results.
newsitem.headline: Incitec sees subdued second half results.

text.p: Incitec Ltd said on Thursday that results for the rest of the 1996/97 year were likely to be subdued.

"...whilst the first half had produced a record outcome, results for the balance of the year were expected to be subdued," the company said in a statement accompanying the release of its first half profit result to March 31.

"International fertilizer markets have weakened substantially over recent months, and those effects are flowing through to domestic markets. Coupled with an intensified competitive environment, our fertilizer business will feel the effects', managing director Jim Babon said.
The company is majority-owned by U.K.-controlled ICI Australia Ltd.
The company said net profit in the first six months of 1996/97 was A$25.52 million from A$25.46 million a year ago.

While the first half dividend was cut to 10 cents per sahre from 15.5 cents, Incitec said it would pay a special dividend of 25 cents per share to release accumulated surplus franking credits to shareholders.
Revenue rose by one percent to A$446.2 million.

"Generally favourable seasonal conditions in the key sugar, grain and cotton growing regions, which underpinned the record 1996 results, supported maintenance of overall sales levels of the businesses aligned to agriculture", Babon said.
He said fertilizer sales volumes were on a par with last year but overall revenue slipped by five percent and sales by the agricultural chemical business, Crop Cars, rose by 14 percent.
Incitec achieved a 50 percent jump in 1995/96 net profit to A$60.08 million from A$40.07 million a year earlier.
